To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following three factors are key to achieving the highest possible performance with a LSTM-CTc based ASR system: 1) use of a larger model, 2) use of data augmentation and 3) use of a regularization technique.

(1) the use of data augmentation can significantly improve the performance of an LSTM-CTC system trained with a small amount of training data, (2) the use of regularization can further improve the performance of the augmented LSTM-CTC systems, and (3) the performance gap between the LSTM-CTC and the Kaldi based DNN-CE systems on the Librispech 100hr (test-clean) corpus is reduced from 5.3% to 2.5

(i) the performance gap between LSTM-CTC and CE-based systems on small data domains can be closed with data augmentation and regularization; (ii) the gap is more pronounced on domains with limited training and development data; and (iii) a well designed LSTM-CTC system is a viable alternative to a strong Kaldi baseline on domains with limited amount of data
